summary: Streaming session duplication and intermittent cross-region egress after residency-lock refresh in Private VPC
environment: prod/eu-west (private VPC peered to us-east for backup egress)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicated chunks in streaming responses and occasional full requests egressing via us-east even though tenant is pinned to eu-west strict residency. This started after enabling automatic residency-lock refresh for their Private VPC deployment (toggle enabled 2026-03-10).

Impact:
- Intermittent duplication of streaming frames visible to client (duplicate partial tokens appearing ~0.5-2% of streams).
- P95 latency spikes (+30-120ms) correlated with duplicated streams.
- Some requests observed in packet captures and flow logs leaving eu-west and reaching us-east edge (unexpected cross-region egress).
- Customer workflow: bank transaction summarization via streaming; duplicates are causing downstream de-dup logic to reject some chunks, causing UI flicker and a small percentage of failed user flows.

Environment:
- VerityBank private deployment hosted in eu-west VPC with peered backup egress to us-east (configured per compliance).
- Residency mode: strict with residency-lock refresh enabled (automatic refresh window = 15m).
- Client: in-house web client using websocket streaming with keepalive 45s.
- Time window first observed: 2026-03-11 10:42 - 2026-03-12 09:00 UTC.

Observed telemetry/logs (snippets attached in comments):
- Edge flow logs show intermittent NAT translations to us-east edge IPs during refresh windows.
- Streaming server logs show duplicate chunk IDs generated by the same request ID but different connection IDs.
- Auth service logs show short-lived token rotation events (STS) coinciding with residency-lock refresh timestamps.

Other notes:
- Customer has packet captures, Cloud NAT logs, and conservative retry logic on the client (single in-flight request per session).
- No large-scale outage; behaviour is sporadic and low volume, but reproducible for this tenant under the lock-refresh schedule.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use VerityBank Private deployment in eu-west with residency-lock refresh enabled (15m window).
2) Open websocket streaming session from a client behind the customer VPC (simulate same egress IP).
3) Trigger a streaming generation workload on rw-open-13b-v1 (moderate token length, ~400 tokens).
4) Observe server-side stream frames and client received frames around the residency lock refresh boundary (e.g., at minute 14-16 of refresh timer).
5) Repeat while collecting edge flow logs and auth token audit logs to correlate timestamps.
comments: 2026-03-12 12:03 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer submitted packet captures and flow logs showing egress to us-east edge IPs during refresh windows. Asked for websocket connection IDs and sampling of server stream logs.

2026-03-12 13:15 UTC - VerityBank (Customer): Provided pcaps and noted that duplicates align with the residency-lock refresh (they can toggle to test). They can reproduce by enabling refresh every 5 minutes in staging.

2026-03-12 16:40 UTC - Michael Chen (SRE): Initial triage — found link between STS token rotation and connection re-binding in our edge tunnel codepath. Creating a controlled test to reproduce in our staging VPC mirror.

2026-03-13 09:02 UTC - Michael Chen (SRE): Repro in staging by forcing lock refresh; observed two connection IDs for same request and duplicate chunk emission when the backend session was handed to a new edge proxy before client reconnect acknowledged the old stream state.

2026-03-13 11:48 UTC - Backend Eng (Leila Gómez): Hypothesis: during residency-lock refresh we momentarily mark the tenant as transferable which triggers ephemeral routing updates; edge proxies race to rebind connection; we may re-emit buffered chunks when new proxy believes it is the primary for the stream.

2026-03-14 07:20 UTC - Michael Chen (SRE): Narrowed to race between token rotation (auth) and route binding TTL. Pushed a feature branch that serializes rebind steps to avoid duplicate emit; running canary in staging full-run against customer's capture set.
2026-03-14 09:05 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer asked whether short-term mitigation exists to avoid duplicates while we validate the fix.

2026-03-14 10:30 UTC - Michael Chen (SRE): Suggested workaround: temporarily disable automatic residency-lock refresh (switch to manual refresh) or increase refresh window beyond client websocket keepalive to avoid overlap (recommended >10m). Also advised adding idempotent dedupe token in streaming payload as short-term client patch.
investigation_notes: - Reproduced locally in staging by toggling residency-lock refresh; duplication rate ~1.2% with 15m window, increases to ~3.8% when forcing 1m window.

- Packet captures show SYN/FIN from proxied connections where mid-stream rebind happens; new edge connection receives buffered messages and replays last N frames without ref counter, causing duplicates at client.
- Auth STS rotation timestamp correlated with edge routing update events in control plane logs (control-plane workflow: mark transferable -> update routing table -> edge subscribes -> rebind).

- Hypothesis: control plane currently treats token rotation and route refresh as independent events; when they overlap, edge proxy may accept ownership while previous session not fully drained, resulting in double-emit of buffered frames.
- Telemetry dashboards referenced: /dashboards/edge/rebind-events, /dashboards/streaming/duplicate-frames (internal links provided to eng team).
- Related runbook: Private VPC Egress Runbook — contains steps to disable automatic refresh and verify route sticky session (linked above).
resolution: Workaround applied: Customer agreed to temporarily disable automatic residency-lock refresh (manual refresh only) and increase websocket keepalive to 90s. This reduced duplicate frames to <0.1% in their staging tests.

Planned fix: engineering to land serialized rebind flow that ensures old edge proxy drains buffered frames and acks before new proxy replays any buffered content. PR branch: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4123 (under review).

Rollout plan: Canary in staging (complete), progressive rollout to eu-west Private clusters over 72 hours with monitoring for duplicate-frame metric and p95 latency regressions. Post-deploy verification with VerityBank capture set scheduled for 2026-03-18.
Follow-ups: add an alert for rebind-events > 0.1% and add documentation entry in Private VPC Runbook about recommended websocket keepalive/refresh window alignment.
